title: Идея отправить маму на балет  (The Idea to Send Mom to the Ballet)

segments.t: Learning that Chef Barinov's romantic evening in the office fell apart, Senya and Fedya joke about TV commercials before suggesting he invite Elena home while his mother is out at the ballet. Inspired, Barinov immediately hatches a plan to clear Lyova's apartment.
Ах ты, бог ты мой, не переживай.
Там в перерывах много чего советуют.
А можно я сегодня уйду пораньше?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'So how did it go?' Opening up candidly in front of Kostya, Max puts the question word "chto" right at the start so Kostya hears the focus immediately.
'It did not work out.' Kostya reacts boldly across the room, watching Max's face to see how the news lands.
Ах ты, бог ты мой, не переживай.
'Oh, good grief, do not worry about it.' Max speaks openly in this beat and uses "perezhivay" ("worry", from "perezhivat") to make the point stick.
'At the end of the day.' Returning to the ends on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 3 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'You watch football on TV, right?' Max questions straight out before Kostya can change the subject.
Там в перерывах много чего советуют.

'They advertise plenty of remedies during the commercial breaks.' Pointing to the break in this beat, Kostya chooses "pereryvakh" ("break, interval", from the root "pereryv") so Max hears the exact meaning.
'I do not need pills!' Focusing on the pill in this beat, Max lands on "tabletki" ("pill, tablet", built on "tabletka") to keep the statement grounded.
'I told you she would never agree to do it here.' Kostya responds quietly facing Max, refusing to let the moment slip past.
'What about inviting her to your home?' Max counters quietly in front of Kostya and uses "priglasit" ("to invite") to carry the main weight of the thought.
'Send your mother where?' Looking over quietly beside Max, Kostya puts the question word "kuda" right at the start so Max hears the focus immediately.

'To the cinema or the ballet, there you go.' Max casually speaks this courtesy word toward Kostya using "pozhaluysta" ("please") — the all-purpose Russian politeness word that covers both "please" and "you're welcome".
'For the entire night?' Bringing up the entire night on the spot, Kostya leans on "noch" ("night") to give the whole sentence its punch.
А можно я сегодня уйду пораньше?

'Could I please leave a little early today?' Weighing in openly in the exchange, Max leans on "mozhno" ("it is possible, one may"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".
Ах ты, бог ты мой, не переживай.
Там в перерывах много чего советуют.
А можно я сегодня уйду пораньше?
That wraps up this scene as senya and Fedya tease Chef Barinov after his failed evening in the office and give him the idea to send Lyova's mother to the ballet for the night. Until next time!
